summary: Tested the eSIM BulkSMS backend only (Node, simulated Spenza provider: WEB_CLOUDIVR_DRY_RUN=true in .env). No real eSIM was bought, no real SMS was sent, nothing was deployed. (1) Engine suite js/tests/test_bulk_esim_engine.js: 26 passed, 0 failed (nodejs stopped while it ran). (2) Bot flow scripts against the live nodejs service: test_bulk_esim_bot_flow.js 13/13 steps OK (booking scheduled, 510 queued, 1 test msg, wallet debited $25.5); test_bulk_esim_bot_pay.js OK (crypto/bank checkout -> digital-product-pay with dpProductKey bulk-esim-sms, paid() -> scheduled). (3) New QA suite js/tests/test_bulk_esim_stop_upload_iter239.js: 32 passed, 0 failed. It covers: the defaults (initialEsims=1, minEsims=1, autoProvision=false, manualApproval=true); autoscale with 0 eSIMs and confirmBooking/autoscale under capacity demand both call P.provision 0 times (only an admin alert); /bulkprovision provisions exactly one; STOP variants (STOP, stopall, ' Unsubscribe ', 'Opt Out', QUIT, cancel, End) create bsSuppression {cid:'*'}, reject queued texts to that number for 2 different customers and brands, and queue a confirmation; sendOne/parseContacts block the number for every customer; processOne rejects a message that was already 'processing' when STOP arrived (opted_out); the confirmation is really sent (system texts skip suppression); STOP from an ambiguous sender (2 owners) still blocks it, and the message is held for review; a routed STOP sets by=cid and notifies the owner; 'please stop by tomorrow' does not block; HELP queues an auto reply; a duplicate webhook (same Message_ID) has no effect; low credit (BULK_ESIM_FAKE_CREDIT=3) pauses sending and alerts the admin, and a top-up resumes it automatically. Contacts upload through bot.handle with a fake msg.document and a stubbed getFileLink served from a local HTTP server: .exe rejected; >2MB rejected; Contacts.CSV parsed into 505 contacts with 1 opted-out number skipped; a bsUploads record is stored (storagePath, text/csv) and the campaign gets uploadId; the object is readable back from Emergent Object Storage; when storage fails (proxy unreachable) the campaign still proceeds with uploadId null; an unreadable file gives a friendly error; pasting still works. Live routing probe: a document message posted to localhost:5000/telegram/webhook while in state bse-contacts reaches the BulkSMS handler ('Couldn't read that file' reply in the nodejs log, because the file_id was fake). (4) Lint: `npx eslint js/bulk-esim/ js/tests/test_bulk_esim_*.js` is clean. `npx eslint js/bulk-esim/ js/tests/` is NOT clean: 228 older problems in unrelated js/tests files, none in BulkSMS files. `node --check js/_index.js` OK. Code review found no path that buys an eSIM unless an admin runs /bulkprovision (provisionOne is called only from /bulkprovision, or from confirmBooking/autoscale when autoProvision && !manualApproval, which is false by default).

minor.issue: STOP with punctuation ('STOP.', 'Stop!', 'STOP ALL') does not match, because the regex requires an exact keyword. The number is not blocked and gets no confirmation. Compliance risk; suggest stripping non-letters before testing the regex.

The suppression is written only after an eSIM with msisdn === x.to and status != 'replaced' is found. A STOP that arrives late to a replaced line, or to a number that is no longer in the pool, is lost (verified: STOP to an unknown platform number -> no block). Suggest writing the global suppression before the eSIM lookup.

Every new STOP (different Message_ID) queues another 'You are unsubscribed' confirmation, and HELP replies are unlimited. Suggest sending the confirmation only when the suppression upsert actually inserted (upsertedCount), and rate-limiting HELP per number.
saveUpload runs before the min-volume check, so files with fewer than 500 numbers (and every retry) leave orphan bsUploads rows and storage objects. The isDeleted flag is never used.
initialEsims is defined and can be set with /bulkset, but no code reads it. It has no effect; only minEsims drives the autoscale alert.

action_items: Make the STOP/HELP matching tolerant of punctuation and whitespace variants (e.g. strip [^a-z ] before the regex; consider 'STOP ALL').
In onWebhook, insert the bsSuppression {cid:'*'} row for STOP before the eSIM lookup or regardless of it, so opt-outs to replaced or unknown lines are not lost.
Queue the STOP confirmation only on the first opt-out (upsertedCount), and rate-limit HELP auto replies.
Optional: save the upload copy only after parseContacts passes minVolume, or clean up orphans.
Add a guard to test_bulk_esim_engine.js: it runs deleteMany({}) on every bs* collection in DB_NAME and would wipe real BulkSMS data if run against a populated DB.
critical_code_review_comments: test_bulk_esim_engine.js wipes all bs* collections without a guard. My new suite refuses to run if any collection holds more than 1 doc; the engine suite should do the same.
storage.js has a hardcoded fallback URL 'https://integrations.emergentagent.com' when INTEGRATION_PROXY_URL is unset (minor).

System texts (STOP confirmations, HELP, loop tests) share the per-eSIM esimPerMin window with customer traffic. With one eSIM at 10/min, a burst of STOPs delays customer sends; acceptable, but worth knowing.

The provider defaults to simulated only through WEB_CLOUDIVR_DRY_RUN=true. Real SPENZA_BULK keys are present in .env, so a non-dry environment would be live: /bulkprovision there spends money (by design, admin only).

success_rate.backend: 100% (26/26 engine + 32/32 new QA + both bot flow scripts OK)

seed_data_creation: None kept. All bs* collections were empty before testing (only the worker bsLocks doc). After the tests I deleted all bs* docs these runs created (bsLocks kept) and reset state 990000111 action to 'none'. 990000111 is the existing QA chat used by E1's scripts; its walletOf was reset by bot_flow to usdIn 100, usdOut 25.5. 2 small test contact files (engine + iter239) remain in Object Storage under cloudivr-bulksms/uploads/ because the API has no delete.
context_for_next_testing_agent: BulkSMS backend = Node supervisor program 'nodejs' (port 5000; webhook /telegram/webhook; Spenza webhook /api/bulk-esim/webhook). Run the engine suite and test_bulk_esim_stop_upload_iter239.js with nodejs stopped (sudo supervisorctl stop nodejs), then start it again. The bot flow and pay scripts need nodejs running. WEB_CLOUDIVR_DRY_RUN=true means simulated provider. Do not read backend/.env directly; check vars via node + dotenv printing only SET/UNSET. Never run /bulkprovision in a non-dry env.
rca of the issue: No blocking bugs. The one early failure in my own suite ('top-up -> sends') was a test artifact: with a single eSIM, the per-eSIM 10/min window was already used up by the 11 STOP/HELP system texts sent that minute, so the text correctly waited (nextAt +5s). The assertion was adjusted.
